accommodate: The new classroom is big enough to accommodate the whole class.
Our small car cannot accommodate five children and all their bags.
Will the shed accommodate a bike, a lawnmower and my old scooter?
accompany: Mum will accompany me to the library on Saturday.
May I accompany you to the park with your dog?
Soft piano music will accompany the choir at the school concert.
according: According to the weather forecast, it will rain all day on Friday.
We are baking the bread according to my gran's old recipe.
The game must be played according to the rules inside the box.
aggressive: My cat can look aggressive when she hisses and puffs up her fur.
A good team plays hard but is never aggressive with the others.
The aggressive goose hissed and chased us away from its pond.
embarrass: Forgetting my lines in the play could embarrass me a lot.
Does it embarrass you when everyone sings happy birthday to you?
Getting a loud round of applause may embarrass a shy child.
harass: Do not harass the cat by asking her to play again and again.
The seagulls harass us at the beach, begging for our chips.
Please do not harass the baker with questions every minute!
occupy: What game can occupy the children on a rainy afternoon?
A big sofa can occupy most of our small living room.
Painting will occupy me for the whole of Saturday morning.
occur: Rainbows occur when the sun shines through falling rain.
When does the school sports day usually occur?
Will the next full moon occur on a Tuesday?
committee: The committee met after school to decide the date of the sports day.
The class committee voted on a name for our new rabbit.
Who is on the committee that picks the books for our library?
necessary: Pack only the necessary things in your bag for the school trip.
It is not necessary to shout, because I can hear you!
Warm boots are necessary for a winter walk through the snow.

rejected.s: Which grown-up can accompany our class on the trip to the seaside?
rejected.reason: checker: A grown-up could also 'occupy' the class on the trip, so the gap is not unique. (also fits: occupy)

rejected.s: Did the shop open at nine, according to the sign on the door?
rejected.reason: checker: Using the past tense 'did' with a sign is awkward and a little confusing for a child.

rejected.s: Please don't embarrass me by waving at me in front of my friends!
rejected.reason: checker: 'Harass me by waving at me' could also work, so the gap is not unique enough. (also fits: harass)

rejected.s: Why do the flies harass us every time we eat outside?
rejected.reason: checker: Flies could jokingly 'accompany' us every time we eat, so the gap is not clearly unique. (also fits: accompany)
